name: The Long Cartography
description: An anthology neural-feed drama in which each season places the viewer in the body of a different person navigating corporate intrigue in the Spire — a Tier 5 logistics executive, a personal security contractor, a synthetic concierge with a malfunctioning loyalty protocol. The show is produced by a small independent studio and licensed through a Vantablack subsidiary on unusually favorable terms, which has made the production team quietly nervous about what they may have agreed to in the fine print.
cultural_impact: The Season 1 finale — in which the viewer-as-executive discovers they have been feeding real proprietary data to an unknown party through the neural-feed interface itself — sparked a brief but intense public debate about BCI content security that Vantablack successfully redirected toward a competitor.
story_hooks: The studio's lead writer has realized that certain details in Season 2's Spire setting — details she invented — are accurate to classified Axiom infrastructure layouts she has no way of knowing.
Someone is distributing a modified version of Season 2 in Axiom territory with the Axiom-banned episode restored and additional scenes inserted that no one at the studio wrote.
The 'unusually favorable' licensing terms the studio signed include a clause granting Vantablack passive read access to all neural-feed sessions — the studio's lawyer has just found it.
